title: Take a ceramic wall hook down: hold it with one hand while the other backs out its single screw
instruction: Take the ceramic hook off the wall without letting it fall. Put the hook, its screw and its washer in the padded tray, and put the screwdriver back in its stand.
context: Painters and maintenance workers remove wall hardware before repainting or repair. Supporting the fragile hook while disengaging its recessed fastener requires coordinated use of both hands.
setup: Simulation specification, not measurements of a purchased specimen. Fixed YAM station layout; x points away from the robot, y left, and heights below are above the tabletop. A fixed painted wooden wall panel is 360 mm wide, 155 mm high and 18 mm thick; its front is at x=300 mm, with two 100 x 40 x 20 mm rear feet. A glazed ceramic knob hook, 60 mm diameter, 42 mm projection, 130 g, is centred at (x,y,height)=(300,0,110) mm. Its 30 mm neck and 5.2 mm through-hole surround a steel M4 screw: 50 mm shank, 8 mm diameter x 3 mm head, with 10 mm engaged thread. The head sits in a 12 mm wide, 6 mm deep recess over a nylon washer (10 mm outer width, 4.6 mm hole, 1.5 mm thick). A cordless pen screwdriver has a plastic body 160 x 18 mm, a 12 mm metal chuck and 30 mm steel bit; overall length 202 mm, mass 90 g. It lies along +x, body centre (200,-210,44) mm, in a fixed polymer stand with a 170 x 50 x 6 mm base and two 14 x 32 mm U rests centred at x=140 and 250 mm, rest floors 35 mm high and cheek tops 47 mm high. A fixed polymer parts tray is centred at (185,240,0) mm, outer size 200 x 250 mm, 70 mm walls, 4 mm wall/base thickness; a 10 mm foam liner puts the support surface 14 mm above the table. The screwdriver starts in its stand; hook, washer and screw start assembled on the wall. All dimensions and collision geometry are specified in task.py; no layout jitter.
scoring: Sequential terminal-state score: 0 while less than 10 mm of screw travel has disengaged the insert; 0.25 once the thread is disengaged; 0.5 when the hook is also at least 20 mm from its initial body-origin position and no damage flag has occurred; 0.75 when the hook also rests in the tray; 1.0 when screw and washer are also in the tray and the screwdriver rests in both stand cradles. Damage proxy: permanently cap at 0.25 after hook downward speed exceeds sqrt(2*9.81*0.02)=0.6264 m/s (even while held), or its collision lower bound is below 4 mm above the table while its origin is outside the tray outer footprint. In-tray means the complete collision bounds fit the 192 x 242 mm inner footprint, with their bottom at least 10 mm and top at most 90 mm above the table. For the hook, its bottom must additionally be within 4 mm of the liner top at 14 mm. Rest means body-origin speed and the maximum speed over the complete collision geometry below 10 mm/s, including rotation, and all gripper/finger collision bounding boxes at least 5 mm clear. Screw and washer may remain in the hook. Driver return requires its body axis within 10 degrees of either x direction, body centre within 20 mm in x of its initial centre, and the body crossing both cradle centres at y within 2 mm and height within 4 mm of the initial 44 mm, with at least 7 mm of body beyond each cradle centre. Full-score conditions must hold for 1 continuous second to terminate successfully. Intermediate credit can decrease if the final state deteriorates.
reset_notes: In simulation, reset the fixed layout and assembled stack using the supplied task reset. A physical analogue would need dimensions checked against the specification, a compatible powered screwdriver, and inspection/replacement of chipped hooks; no physical trial is claimed.
fidelity: Rigid-body contacts; coded thread releases after 10 mm with tip alignment within 2.5 mm radial, -3 to +1.5 mm axial and 10 degrees; withdrawal <=2.8 mm/s. No rotation, torque, thread contact, fracture, foam compliance, paint adhesion or thread-locker. Hook uses box colliders; washer a square ring. Damage uses the stated speed/table-proximity proxy, not free-fall or impact force. Release uses native hand poses and conservative URDF bounds. Full limitations are in README.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2,400 steps, max_steps); scripted demo: 1.0 (718 steps, success, 35.9 s). Both use the same final task/scorer revision and instruction, seed 0, fixed layout.
